Paragraph: At this time the assembly of celestials told Brahma of their troubles. "Oh Lord! A rakshasa by name Ravana armed with the boon granted by you is tormenting us. His diabolic powers leave us powerless. Unable to chastise him and honoring the boon granted by you, we bear the havoc that he creates. With arrogance born of that power the evil demon makes the three worlds tremble with fear. Rendered invincible he spares neither asuras, Brahmins or gandharvas. We dread him. Even the Sun shines subdued, the winds dare not to blow and the restless oceans still at his appearance".
Chapter/Canto/Verse_Reference: Bala Kanda, Chapter 15 (Lamentation of the Devas)
Situation/Problem_Faced: The celestials are facing severe torment from the powerful Rakshasa, Ravana, who has been granted a boon of invincibility by Brahma. This boon renders them helpless to stop his atrocities, leading to widespread fear and chaos in the three worlds.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: The passage highlights the consequences of unbridled power when wielded by an unrighteous being. It introduces the concept of a divine boon becoming a source of suffering due to its misuse. It also sets up the problem that necessitates divine intervention in the narrative, illustrating how even powerful gods can be constrained by their own granted boons.
Outcome/Resolution: The celestials formally present their grievous problem to Lord Brahma, seeking a solution to Ravana's tyranny, which has rendered them powerless due to Brahma's own boon. This appeal is a crucial step towards the eventual incarnation of Vishnu to defeat Ravana.
Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The celestials' plea to Brahma underscores the disruption of Dharma and Cosmic Order by Ravana's unrighteous actions, made possible by a divine Boon (Vara). This situation highlights the concept of Adharma manifesting through misuse of power, creating widespread suffering despite divine constraints. It sets the spiritual stage for a necessary divine intervention to restore balance and rectify the consequences of a boon's exploitation.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Psychologically, the passage vividly portrays the intense fear and terror experienced by the celestials due to Ravana's unchecked power. Their feeling of powerlessness and helplessness in the face of his 'diabolic powers' creates profound distress and suffering. Their act of appealing to Brahma represents a coping mechanism of seeking relief and intervention from a higher authority when overwhelmed by an external threat, illustrating a collective psychological crisis.
